title: South Korea to inspect all exam takers’ glasses following AI cheating scandal | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

South Korea will inspect all glasses worn by students taking itsnational college entrance exam this week, after thetop scorer on another notoriously difficult test confessed he used AI to cheat, shaking confidence in the country’s strict examination process.

The cheating scandal prompted Prime Minister Han Sung-sook to call officials to a meeting on Monday, where the country’s education ministry was ordered to ensure test takers hand in their smart devices before exams.

Education minister Choi Kyo-jin told parliament there would be “a thorough inspection of all glasses in each test session to ensure a fair and safe testing environment.” Smart glasses have been added to a list of items prohibited inside the testing room,he said, adding that the consequences of cheating using smart devices could include criminal punishment.

This Thursday, around 550,000 students are expected to sit the country’sinfamous College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), an arduous eight-hour exam that is seen as a barometer for future success and social status in hyper-competitive South Korea.

Each year the test brings the country to a standstill, with flights banned from taking off or landing during the half-hour-long listening comprehension section to ensure there are no distractions.

The changes to exam rules come one day after the top scoring student in the country’s accounting exam confessed to cheating, following months of scrutiny over his suspiciously high score.

In a video published online Sunday, the student said he had cheated using a miniature camera, his phone and AI, adding he had confessed to Seoul police about the fraud.

“I cheated on the tax accountant exam. I sincerely apologize for causing damage to a lot of people,” he said in the video.

He referenced the upcoming college entrance exam, warning “if there is someone thinking of cheating like I did, I’m going to tell the investigators everything, so I hope you don’t think that you won’t get caught.”

Students have found ways to cheat on tests since the dawn of time, but the rise of AI has made deception slicker and more sophisticated. Smart glasses with integrated AI engines, built-in cameras, microphones, speakers and sensors have become tools for cheating.

While old-fashioned cheating may have required craning your neck for a quick peek at your neighbor’s answers, a test taker wearing AI glasses can simply glance at a question and have the answer fed back to them in a matter of seconds.

Once reserved for tech nerds, the devices are quickly moving into the mainstream. US tech giant Metalaunched its first AI-enabled glasses with Ray-Ban in late 2023, and has since released several new versions. Last year alone, more than seven million pairs were sold.

The new technology has becomeespecially problematic in East Asia’s test-obsessed societies,where students have turned to smart glasses and AI glasses to get an upper hand, forcing governments to take strict measures.

Earlier this year in South Korea, two students taking an exam to assess their English language skills — the results of which are often used to make hiring decisions — were caught using smart glasses.

In Taiwan, a student sitting for an entrance exam for a top medical school was discovered wearing smart glasses after proctors noticed the student staring oddly at the test, leading to an inspection that revealed the frame was emitting heat.

For China’sgrueling annual college entrance examin June – which more than 10 million hopefuls take each year – authorities required screening of all glasses.

John Liu contributed reporting.

John Liu contributed reporting.
